references.text: God made a covenant with Israel at Sinai/Horeb, promising that they would be his treasured people if they kept his covenant.
Moses sprinkled the blood on the people and confirmed the covenant that the Lord had made with Israel at Sinai.
Moses was on the mountain for forty days, and the Lord wrote the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments, on the tablets.
The Lord announced his covenant to Israel at Horeb and wrote the Ten Commandments on two stone tablets.
A reference to the covenant that the Lord made with Israel at Horeb, in addition to the covenant in Moab.
The ark of the covenant contained the two stone tablets that Moses placed at Horeb, where the Lord made a covenant with Israel.
The prophet Malachi reminds Israel of the law of Moses given at Horeb, with all its statutes and laws.
Paul uses Mount Sinai as an illustration of the old covenant made with Israel.
Hebrews quotes Jeremiah and refers to the covenant God made with the fathers when he brought them out of Egypt.
